messages:
marta_design: tossed up a micro-proposal for a compact 'change tool' flow in run history. idea: inline one-line sig + small 'Change' button that expands a lightweight picker. mock: https://redwood.mock/s/compact-change.png
ryan_devex: looks good. question: when the sig preview expands, should it push the rest of the feed down or float? I lean push (keeps vertical rhythm predictable).
tori_accessibility: accessibility nits: if we push, ensure focus follows the expansion. add `aria-live=\"polite\"` region announcing \"Signature expanded\" and the chevron has aria-expanded. keyboard: support Enter/Space to toggle and Arrow keys to move between inline controls.
sam_engineer: implementation constraints: pushing is simpler for mobile; floating panel would need portal logic and focus management. lazy-load schemas on expand and cache by id. ps: avoid loading full diff renderer unless user opens full inspector.
aya_research: from prototypes, users prefer inline for quick confirms. we should include a tiny provenance line: \"original: toolX → current: toolY (@marta_design, 3m ago)\" so audit info is visible without opening inspector.
marta_design: copy candidates: 
- button: \"Change\" vs \"Edit tool\" vs \"Change tool\"
- preview label: \"sig: summarize(text: string) -> {summary: string}\"
- toast after change: \"Tool updated — rerun to apply\" vs auto-rerun
ryan_devex: prefer short button \"Change\" (less visual weight). prefer toast that doesn't auto-run. give a CTA: \"Rerun\" in toast.
tori_accessibility: microcopy: include context in aria-labels, e.g., `aria-label=\"Change tool for invocation at 11:12\"` so screen reader users understand which run item it affects.
